title: Water Damage Mitigation: Holding Several Jobs at Once
content:
**Customer account terms — Water Damage Mitigation**

A customer may hold any number of water mitigation jobs at the same time, one for each separate loss; landlords, property managers, associations and commercial owners routinely carry several open jobs across their properties. Each job is a separate contract with its own tier, authorization, ledger and invoice.

## What the term means in practice
| Question | Answer under these terms |
|---|---|
| Is there a maximum number of Water Damage Mitigation jobs per customer? | No. The company sets no limit on how many jobs one customer holds. |
| What separates one job from another? | Each job answers a separate loss. |
| What does each job carry for itself? | Its own tier, its own work authorization, its own ledger of charges and payments, and its own invoice. |

## Illustration (hypothetical)
A property manager responsible for three apartment buildings reports a burst supply line in one building and a roof leak in another. Each loss is a separate loss, so each is held as its own Water Damage Mitigation job, each with its own tier fixed from that loss, its own signed authorization, its own ledger and its own invoice.
